- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast dip depth or add slight upward bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots downward — cap forecast decline to 3–5% below peak or align with 10-day moving average.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (avg between -0.3 and +0.3), model frequently overestimates mean reversion — adjust downward by 1–2% for 3–5 day horizon.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often underestimates volatility in early days — increase initial forecast by 0.5–1.5% if sentiment is volatile or negative.
- When sentiment shows strong upward momentum (avg > +0.3), model tends to lag — add 1–2% buffer to forecast to account for delayed reaction.
- If recent sentiment is negative but price is trending upward, model often fails to recognize reversal — reduce forecast slope or add 1–2% upward bias to counteract sentiment lag.
